newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha softer due to crudes, arbitrage lots.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha softer due to crudes, arbitrage lots.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices fell for the third consecutive business day in afternoon trade on Tuesday due to weaker crudes as well as talk of arbitrage cargoes heading to Asia, traders said.
Expectations of slower physical demand for May cargoes were another bearish factor in the market, they said.
Activity was generally subdued as Japanese traders were taking a breather from an active buying spell last week.
Offers for second-half May open-spec naphtha were heard at $228.00 per tonne with no bids having surfaced. It was quoted at $229.50/230.00 in late Monday trading.
First-half June was indicated at about $224.00/226.00, down from Monday's $227.00/228.00.
The one-month spread from first-half May was notionally quoted at plus $2.50/4.00, narrower than Monday's $3.50/4.50.
In physical trading, a South Korean petrochemical firm said it had bought a first-half May arrival cargo at around $3.00 over the mean of Japanese quotes late last week.

The deal has concluded the company's spot cargo procurement for May as requirements for the second half of the month will be covered by term cargoes, a naphtha trader with the company said. --Tokyo Energy Desk +81-3-3432-8837
